summary: Seke-Banza territory (Kongo-Central, between Matadi and Boma north of the Congo river) contains Seke-Banza centre, the Kitsiengo/Mbenza Thubi agglomeration, the Inga hydroelectric site and rural villages of the Seke-Banza and Inga health zones. No armed group holds territory here; the area is far from the eastern conflict zones. Towns are policed by the PNC with territorial administration and customary chiefs handling disputes; the Inga dam complex is a strategic site with additional FARDC/state security deployment. Past Bundu dia Kongo (BDK/BDM) political unrest in Kongo-Central did not displace state control. Web search was unavailable in this run (search budget exhausted), so the assessment rests on default state presence.

zones.description: Seke-Banza territorial centre, Kitsiengo (Mbenza Thubi) agglomeration and Kizulu Tunga/Nsanda – larger towns
zones.evidence: Larger towns with no reported armed-group control; PNC commissariats and territorial administration handle policing, arrests and detention. No sources could be retrieved in this run.

zones.description: Inga hydroelectric site and workers' cités (Inga health area: Fuamalo, Kinshasa 1)
zones.evidence: Strategic dam site and SNEL residential cités under state control; police handle ordinary order while FARDC/state security elements guard the installations. Which force dominates day-to-day is not confirmed by sources in this run.

zones.description: Rural villages of Seke-Banza and Inga health zones
zones.evidence: Rural Bas-Fleuve villages with no reported armed-group activity; state police posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs are the default authority. No sources could be retrieved in this run.
